rows.en: Derock: "You want to hear another of my lectures.
I don't mind. Let's begin."
Ask about the Kingdom of Agarthia
Ask about another country
Never mind
Ask about the Zigrim Republic
Ask about another country
The previous topic...
Ask about York
The previous topic...
That's enough.
Derock: "Understood. If you want to know more,
you can ask me anything."
Derock: "All right, listen carefully.
This country bears the same name as the world itself,
and originally ruled the whole world.
Its capital is called Shangria.
It has split apart several times, and the Dark Ages brought a break,
but it boasts a history of 3,000 years.
Even now, its territory covers roughly half the continent,
and it plays the leading role in this world.
It's a moderate constitutional monarchy, but because of its history,
neighboring countries often view it
with a somewhat critical eye.
It consists of 18 municipalities. Of these, 12 cities
have the right to dissolve and elect the Agarthian Council,
and are called the '12 elector cities.'
Within its borders is a region called the 'Holy Land,'
which is treated as an independent territory.
Incidentally, the Holy Land is the Alchemists' headquarters:
a school, a research institute and a workshop.
It was originally founded to guard against misuse of Alchemy,
with the aim of 'cooperating for the sound development of technology.'
That was its purpose.
It's free from the influence of any national government,
an inviolable sanctuary where every country is forbidden to use force.
That's what it is.
That concludes the explanation."
Derock: "All right, listen carefully.
It gained independence from the Kingdom of Agarthia during the wars 1,800 years ago.
That was how the country began.
Its strength and territory are second only to the Kingdom of Agarthia.
It was originally a monarchy, but a revolution 1,050 years ago
turned it into a republic.
At the time, it came under various pressures from the Kingdom of Agarthia,
and has fought the Kingdom of Agarthia many times since.
Its political acumen and intelligence organizations surpass the Kingdom of Agarthia's.
They're more advanced.
Its military has also been modernizing, and its strength
is widely recognized. With a mixture of contempt and fear,
it's called the 'Wild Valor of the West.'
The head of state is the president, currently Nell Horem.
The president is elected
by popular vote, but the military has great influence.
It would be no exaggeration to say General Growster
holds the real power.
That concludes the explanation."
Derock: "Hmm, that's a very good question.
It's said to have originated with a people who once
settled there, and the area's ancient name became
the country's name. It's a matrilineal nation, so of course its head of state
is a queen. Unlike the Kingdom of Agarthia, it has
an absolute monarchy.
Its territory isn't very large, but its fertile land
and veins of precious minerals have made it a target
of invasion time and again, leading it to build
an insular society. York also has people who swear loyalty to the queen herself,
called the 'Three Sword Knights.'
It would be no exaggeration to say
they're the ones protecting this country.
It has advanced technology, with a different lineage from the Holy Land's Armored Mechs.
Using that technology, it builds
its own Armored Mechs.
Every country acknowledges the performance of York's Armored Mechs,
but their numbers are small, and it has nothing you could call an army.
Still, there's a knight who holds the title 'Sword Radiance,' one of only three on the continent:
Garyud Via Vratzen.
He's truly a 'guardian deity.' Since he began protecting the kingdom,
no country has openly sent troops against it.
It's a small elite force indeed. Its defeat by Zigrim
came from several unfortunate circumstances coinciding.
Queen Alforina was a fine person.
...That concludes the explanation."
